subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of an affine plane spanned by an orthonormal frame is the image of Lebesgue measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let w = (w_0, …, w_{m−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (= Euclid P), a ∈ ℝ^P, and S := {y ∈ ℝ^P : y − a ∈ span(w_0, …, w_{m−1})}, the affine m-plane through a spanned by w. Let ℝ^m := Fin m → ℝ carry the product Lebesgue measure Lᵐ (volume) and j : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, j(z) := a + Σ_i z_i w_i. Then (i) the image measure j_*(Lᵐ) equals Hᵐ⌞S, where Hᵐ = μHE[m]; (ii) S is closed; (iii) (Hᵐ⌞S)(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (iv) (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(a)) > 0 for every r > 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (w : Fin m → Euclid P) (a : Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ w → Measure.map (fun z : Fin m → ℝ => a + ∑ i, z i • w i) volume = (μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)} ∧ IsClosed {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)} ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)}) K < ∞) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 < ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)}) (ball a r)

Source: step 0 of the supplied proof of dmcbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat (word for word the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat) ("ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, ι(z) := Σ_j z_j v_j, a linear isometry onto V₀; Hⁿ⌞V₀ = ι_*(Lⁿ) (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume)"), stated for an arbitrary affine plane and with the local finiteness and positivity used in steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 of that proof. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cbr_cipi_affine_plane_measure (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.cycle_im-a1.plane_integer-a1.plane_measure-a1, status accepted, candidate 21dd628c), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Write Euclid m := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) (Euclidean norm) and toLp : (Fin m → ℝ) → Euclid m for the identity on coordinates (WithLp.toLp 2).

1. (Isometric parametrisation.) Define J : Euclid m → ℝ^P, J(u) := a + Σ_i u_i w_i. For c ∈ Euclid m, orthonormality gives ⟨Σ_i c_i w_i, Σ_i c_i w_i⟩ = Σ_i c_i² (Orthonormal.inner_sum), and Σ_i c_i² = ‖c‖² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq); since both norms are ≥ 0, ‖Σ_i c_i w_i‖ = ‖c‖. Hence ‖J(u) − J(u′)‖ = ‖Σ_i (u_i − u′_i) w_i‖ = ‖u − u′‖, i.e. J is an isometry (Isometry.of_dist_eq).

2. (Range.) range(J) = S. Indeed y = J(u) iff y − a = Σ_i u_i w_i; conversely, if y − a ∈ span(w) then y − a = Σ_i c_i w_i for some c : Fin m → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun, Fin m being finite), and y = J(toLp c).

3. (Hausdorff measure under the isometry.) For an isometry, the image of μHE[m] is μHE[m] restricted to the range (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), and μHE[m] on Euclid m is the Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). By step 2, J_*(L_Euclid) = Hᵐ⌞S, where L_Euclid is the Lebesgue measure (volume) of Euclid m.

4. (Proof of (i).) j = J ∘ toLp, and toLp is measure preserving from the product Lebesgue measure of Fin m → ℝ to the Lebesgue measure of Euclid m (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). Both maps are continuous, hence measurable, so j_*(Lᵐ) = J_*(toLp_*(Lᵐ)) = J_*(L_Euclid) = Hᵐ⌞S (Measure.map_map and step 3).

5. (Proof of (ii).) S is the preimage of the linear subspace span(w) under the continuous map y ↦ y − a; span(w) is finite-dimensional, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). So S is closed (and in particular Borel).

6. (Proof of (iii).) Let K be compact; K is closed, hence Borel, so by step 3 (Hᵐ⌞S)(K) = J_*(L_Euclid)(K) = L_Euclid(J⁻¹(K)) (Measure.map_apply). An isometry defined on a complete space is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), so J⁻¹(K) is compact (IsClosedEmbedding.isCompact_preimage), and compact sets have finite Lebesgue measure. Hence (Hᵐ⌞S)(K) < ∞.

7. (Proof of (iv).) Let r > 0. As in step 6, (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(a)) = L_Euclid(J⁻¹(B_r(a))). The set J⁻¹(B_r(a)) is open (J is continuous) and contains 0 because J(0) = a. Nonempty open sets have positive Lebesgue measure (IsOpen.measure_pos; L_Euclid is an additive Haar measure, also for m = 0, where Euclid 0 is a single point of measure 1). Hence (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(a)) > 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: J(u) = a + Σ_i u_i w_i is an isometry of Euclid m onto S (orthonormality: ‖Σ c_i w_i‖ = ‖c‖; range by mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
J_*(Lebesgue) = μHE[m]⌞S by Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume; composing with the measure-preserving toLp gives (i).
S is the preimage of a finite-dimensional (closed) subspace, so closed.
(Hᵐ⌞S)(K) = Leb(J⁻¹K) < ∞ since J is a closed embedding; (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(a)) = Leb(J⁻¹B_r(a)) > 0 since this open set contains 0.

Norms on ℝ^{d+1} are sup norms (only used for boundedness).

1. (Support bound.) tsupport g is compact, hence bounded: tsupport g ⊆ B̄_R(0) for some R ∈ ℝ. If ‖z‖ > R then z ∉ tsupport g, so g(z) = 0; and since tsupport(Dg) ⊆ tsupport g (tsupport_fderiv_subset), also Dg(z) = 0.

2. (Coordinate lines.) For i ∈ Fin (d+1) and y ∈ ℝ^d let ℓ(s) := insertNth i s y ∈ ℝ^{d+1} (i-th coordinate s, coordinate i.succAbove k equal to y_k). Checking coordinates, ℓ(s) = ℓ(0) + s·e_i, so ℓ is affine with derivative e_i, and |s| = |ℓ(s)_i| ≤ ‖ℓ(s)‖. By the chain rule h(s) := g(ℓ(s)) is differentiable with h′(s) = Dg(ℓ(s))(e_i) = ∂_i g(ℓ(s)) for every s ∈ ℝ.

3. (Behaviour of h.) If |s| > |R| then ‖ℓ(s)‖ > R, so h(s) = 0 and h′(s) = 0 by step 1. Hence h → 0 at −∞ and at +∞ (it is eventually 0), and h′ is continuous (g is C¹) with support in [−|R|, |R|], hence integrable on ℝ.

4. (Fubini.) The map z ↦ (z_i, removeNth i z) is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence ℝ^{d+1} → ℝ × ℝ^d (MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove, volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove) whose inverse is (s, y) ↦ insertNth i s y. The function G := 1_H·∂_i g is integrable on ℝ^{d+1}: ∂_i g is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply) and H is Borel. Hence G ∘ (inverse) is integrable for the product measure (MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb), and by change of variables and Fubini (MeasurePreserving.integral_comp′, integral_prod_symm):
   ∫_H ∂_i g = ∫ G = ∫_{y∈ℝ^d} ( ∫_{s∈ℝ} G(insertNth i s y) ds ) dy.

5. (Proof of (a).) Let i ≠ 0. Then d ≥ 1 (Fin 1 has only the element 0), and 0 = i.succAbove 0 (Fin.succAbove_ne_zero_zero), so (insertNth i s y)_0 = y_0 does not depend on s. For fixed y the inner integral is therefore 0 if y_0 ≥ t, and equals ∫_ℝ h′(s) ds if y_0 < t, where h is the function of step 2 for this i and y. By steps 2–3 and the fundamental theorem of calculus on ℝ (integral_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto), ∫_ℝ h′ = 0 − 0 = 0. Thus every inner integral vanishes and ∫_H ∂_i g = 0.

6. (Proof of (b).) Let i = 0. Then insertNth 0 s y = Fin.cons s y (Fin.insertNth_zero′) has 0-th coordinate s, so for fixed y the inner integral is ∫_{s<t} h′(s) ds = ∫_{(−∞, t)} h′ = ∫_{(−∞, t]} h′ (a point is Lebesgue-null; integral_Iic_eq_integral_Iio). Source: Fact (O) and consequence (O1) of the supplied proof of dmcbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat (word for word the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat) ("if v = (v_1, …, v_k) is orthonormal then |α(v)| ≤ |α| (extend v to an orthonormal basis; the k! permutations of (1, …, k) already contribute k!α(v)²)"). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le (DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_eval_le-a1, status accepted, candidate b7846b6), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Its formalization follows exactly this argument: in its own branch it cites the accepted sibling regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis (steps 1–2), which is proved from that node's accepted children regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basis_invariant (step 1) and regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basisFun (step 2). These prerequisites come with its candidate commit, so no edge is declared here. Write Q(f) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})² for an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P, and e for the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).

1. (Q does not depend on the orthonormal basis.) Let b, b′ be orthonormal bases and c(i, s) := ⟨b′_s, b_i⟩, so b_i = Σ_s c(i, s) b′_s. Multilinearity gives α(b∘j) = Σ_{a : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_k c(j(k), a(k))) α(b′∘a). Squaring and summing over j, the j-sum factors over the slots: Σ_j Π_k c(j(k), a(k)) c(j(k), a′(k)) = Π_k Σ_i c(i, a(k)) c(i, a′(k)), and Σ_i c(i, s) c(i, s′) = ⟨b′_s, b′_{s′}⟩ = δ_{ss′} (Parseval for b, orthonormality of b′). Hence all cross terms with a ≠ a′ vanish and Q(b) = Σ_a α(b′∘a)² = Q(b′).

2. (Q(e) = n!|α|².) Terms with non-injective j vanish (an alternating form vanishes on a tuple with two equal entries). Every injective j is uniquely I∘σ with I strictly increasing and σ a permutation of Fin n (I enumerates range(j) increasingly), and α(e∘(I∘σ)) = sgn(σ)α(e∘I), whose square is α(e∘I)². So Q(e) = Σ_{I increasing} n!·α(e∘I)² = n!|α|² by the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm.

3. (Extension of τ.) Orthonormal vectors are linearly independent, so n ≤ P, and τ extends to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f(ι(k)) = τ_k for k ∈ Fin n, where ι := Fin.castLE (n ≤ P) is injective.

4. (Comparison.) For each permutation π of Fin n, j := ι∘π is injective, the maps π ↦ ι∘π are pairwise distinct, and α(f∘(ι∘π)) = α(τ∘π) = sgn(π)α(τ), whose square is α(τ)². All other terms of Q(f) are squares, hence ≥ 0. Therefore n!·α(τ)² ≤ Q(f) = Q(e) = n!|α|² (steps 1–2), so α(τ)² ≤ |α|² and |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (both sides ≥ 0). For n = 0 the family τ is empty, the only j is the empty map and the statement reads |α(())| ≤ |α(())|. ∎
proof_key_steps: Σ_j α(f∘j)² is independent of the orthonormal basis f (multilinear expansion and Parseval).
For the standard basis it equals n!|α|² (alternation and the increasing-index/permutation decomposition).
Extending τ to an orthonormal basis, the n! permuted copies of τ contribute n!α(τ)² ≤ n!|α|².

subproblems.title: A unit covector attaining 1 on an orthonormal frame: |β_τ|_E = 1 and β_τ(τ) = 1
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P. Then there is an n-covector β on ℝ^P with |β|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm β = 1 and β(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) = 1.

Source: consequence (O2) of Fact (O) in the supplied proof of dmcbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat (word for word the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat): "β_v(u) := det(⟨u_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is a k-covector (multilinear and alternating in u) with β_v(v) = 1 and |β_v| = 1 (in a basis extending v its only non-zero values are ±1 on the permutations of (1, …, k))". This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one (DAG node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_norming-a1, status accepted, candidate baaca6e), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Notation: for an n-covector γ on ℝ^P and an orthonormal basis f = (f_0, …, f_{P−1}) of ℝ^P put Q_γ(f) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} γ(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})²; e is the standard basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun); |γ| = covectorEuclideanNorm γ = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} γ(e∘I)²)^{1/2}.

1. (Q_γ does not depend on the orthonormal basis.) Let b, b′ be orthonormal bases and c(i, s) := ⟨b′_s, b_i⟩, so b_i = Σ_s c(i, s) b′_s. Multilinearity gives γ(b∘j) = Σ_{a : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_k c(j(k), a(k))) γ(b′∘a). Squaring and summing over j, the j-sum factors over the slots: Σ_j Π_k c(j(k), a(k)) c(j(k), a′(k)) = Π_k Σ_i c(i, a(k)) c(i, a′(k)), and Σ_i c(i, s) c(i, s′) = ⟨b′_s, b′_{s′}⟩ = δ_{ss′} (Parseval for b, orthonormality of b′). Hence all cross terms with a ≠ a′ vanish and Q_γ(b) = Σ_a γ(b′∘a)² = Q_γ(b′).

2. (Q_γ(e) = n!|γ|².) Terms with non-injective j vanish (an alternating form vanishes on a tuple with two equal entries). Every injective j is uniquely I∘σ with I strictly increasing and σ a permutation of Fin n (I enumerates range(j) increasingly), and γ(e∘(I∘σ)) = sgn(σ)γ(e∘I), whose square is γ(e∘I)². So Q_γ(e) = Σ_{I strictly increasing} n!·γ(e∘I)² = n!|γ|².

3. (Definition of β.) For u = (u_0, …, u_{n−1}) let β(u) := det(⟨u_i, τ_l⟩)_{i,l ∈ Fin n}. The entries of row i are linear in u_i, and the determinant is multilinear and alternating in its rows, so β is multilinear and alternating; on the finite-dimensional space (ℝ^P)^n it is continuous. Hence β is an n-covector.

4. (β(τ) = 1.) ⟨τ_i, τ_l⟩ = δ_{il} by orthonormality, so β(τ) = det(I_n) = 1.

5. (Values on a basis extending τ.) Orthonormal vectors are linearly independent, so n ≤ P, and τ extends to an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P with f(ι(k)) = τ_k for k ∈ Fin n, where ι := Fin.castLE (n ≤ P) is injective. For j : Fin n → Fin P the matrix of β(f∘j) has entries ⟨f_{j(i)}, τ_l⟩ = ⟨f_{j(i)}, f_{ι(l)}⟩ = δ_{j(i), ι(l)}. If some j(i) ∉ range(ι), row i is zero and β(f∘j) = 0. If j is not injective, two rows coincide and β(f∘j) = 0. Otherwise j = ι∘π for a permutation π of Fin n (the maps π ↦ ι∘π being pairwise distinct), the matrix is a permutation matrix and β(f∘j) = sgn(π) = ±1.

6. (|β| = 1.) By step 5, Q_β(f) = Σ_π 1 = n!. By steps 1 and 2, Q_β(f) = Q_β(e) = n!|β|². Hence n!|β|² = n!, so |β|² = 1 and |β| = 1 because |β| ≥ 0. For n = 0 this reads: β is the constant covector 1 (determinant of the empty matrix), the only j is the empty map, β(()) = 1 and |β| = |β(())| = 1. Together with step 4 this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Q_β(f) := Σ_j β(f∘j)² is independent of the orthonormal basis f and equals n!|β|² for the standard basis (multilinear expansion with Parseval; alternation and the increasing-index/permutation decomposition).
β(u) := det(⟨u_i, τ_l⟩) is a continuous alternating n-linear form with β(τ) = det I = 1.
On an orthonormal basis extending τ, β(f∘j) is ±1 exactly for j = ι∘π and 0 otherwise, so Q_β(f) = n!.
Hence n!|β|² = n! and |β| = 1.

subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple (IMRep U m) with weight R.measure = (Hᵐ⌞M) withDensity θ (Hᵐ = μHE[m], θ : ℝ^P → ℕ), S ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set and c > 0 a real number. Assume (Hᵐ⌞S)(K) < ∞ for every compact K, (Hᵐ⌞S)(B_r(x)) > 0 for some x ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ, and R.measure(G) = c·(Hᵐ⌞S)(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P (c read as ENNReal.ofReal c). Then c is a natural number: c = k for some k ∈ ℕ.

Source: steps 5 and 6 of the supplied proof of dmcbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat (word for word the supplied proof of cbr_ci_plane_multiplicity_nat) ("the Borel measures R.measure and θ₀H^d⌞L_t agree on all open sets … so R.measure = θ₀H^d⌞L_t (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion)"; "θ′ = θ₀ H^d-a.e. on D ∩ M_t (ae_eq_of_forall_setLIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite) … θ′ takes values in ℕ, so θ₀ = θ′(x) ∈ ℕ"), for a general Borel set S in place of the plane L_t and a general ball in place of B_1(tv_1). This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cbr_cipi_imrep_weight_const_nat (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.cycle_im-a1.plane_integer-a1.weight_nat-a1, status accepted, candidate 6c348627), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. Write ν := Hᵐ⌞S, M := R.carrier (Borel), θ := R.mult (measurable, ℕ-valued).

1. (Finiteness on balls.) For every ball, ν(B_ρ(z)) ≤ ν(B̄_ρ(z)) < ∞, because closed balls of ℝ^P are compact.

2. (R.measure = c·ν.) The open subsets of ℝ^P form a π-system (isPiSystem_isOpen) generating the Borel σ-algebra (BorelSpace.measurable_eq). The open balls B_{j+1}(0), j ∈ ℕ, cover ℝ^P (iUnion_ball_nat_succ) and R.measure(B_{j+1}(0)) = c·ν(B_{j+1}(0)) < ∞ by the hypothesis and step 1. By hypothesis R.measure and c·ν agree on every open set, so by the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on a generating π-system with a finite cover (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion), R.measure = c·ν.

3. (A set of positive finite measure.) Let x, r be as in the hypothesis and D := S ∩ B_r(x), a Borel set. Then Hᵐ(D) = ν(B_r(x)) (Measure.restrict_apply), so 0 < Hᵐ(D) < ∞ by the hypothesis and step 1.

4. (Formula for the weight.) For Borel E, R.measure(E) = ∫_E θ d(Hᵐ⌞M) = ∫_{E∩M} θ dHᵐ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict).

5. (D is essentially inside M.) By step 4, R.measure(D \ M) = ∫_{(D\M)∩M} θ dHᵐ = 0, since (D \ M) ∩ M = ∅. By step 2 and D \ M ⊆ S, R.measure(D \ M) = c·Hᵐ((D \ M) ∩ S) = c·Hᵐ(D \ M). As c > 0 (so ENNReal.ofReal c ≠ 0), Hᵐ(D \ M) = 0, and therefore Hᵐ(D ∩ M) = Hᵐ(D) > 0 (measure_inter_add_diff).

6. (θ = c almost everywhere on D ∩ M.) Let μ′ := Hᵐ⌞(D ∩ M), a finite measure since μ′(ℝ^P) = Hᵐ(D ∩ M) = Hᵐ(D) < ∞. For every Borel E, using steps 4 and 2, D ⊆ S, and Hᵐ((E ∩ D) \ M) ≤ Hᵐ(D \ M) = 0:
   ∫_E θ dμ′ = ∫_{E∩D∩M} θ dHᵐ = R.measure(E ∩ D) = c·Hᵐ(E ∩ D ∩ S) = c·Hᵐ(E ∩ D) = c·Hᵐ(E ∩ D ∩ M) = ∫_E c dμ′.
   The functions x ↦ (θ(x) : [0, ∞]) and the constant c are measurable and μ′ is σ-finite, so θ = c μ′-almost everywhere (ae_eq_of_forall_setLIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite).

7. (Conclusion.) μ′ ≠ 0 because μ′(ℝ^P) = Hᵐ(D ∩ M) > 0 (step 5), so the almost-everywhere filter of μ′ is non-trivial (ae_neBot) and there is a point y with (θ(y) : [0, ∞]) = ENNReal.ofReal c. Taking real parts (c ≥ 0, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal) gives c = θ(y) with θ(y) ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: R.measure and c·Hᵐ⌞S agree on the π-system of open sets and are finite on the balls B_{j+1}(0), so they are equal.
For D = S ∩ B_r(x): 0 < Hᵐ(D) < ∞ and R.measure(D \ M) = 0 forces Hᵐ(D \ M) = 0, so Hᵐ(D ∩ M) > 0.
Set-lintegrals of θ and of the constant c agree on every Borel set for the finite measure Hᵐ⌞(D ∩ M), so θ = c a.e. there.
A point of the non-null set where θ = c gives c = θ(y) ∈ ℕ.

- V₀ := span(range v) and H_t := {y : ⟨y, v_0⟩ < t}.
- L_t := {y : y − t v_0 ∈ span(range(Fin.tail v))}, where Fin.tail v = (v_1, …, v_d).
- dφ := exteriorDerivative φ, and ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply).
Introduce (SL), P, d, v (orthonormal), θ₀ > 0, C with C(ω) = θ₀∫_{V₀}ω(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) for every test n-form ω, and the ISP hypothesis on C.

0. (Stokes on V₀ and on its half-planes.) The first two hypotheses of (HB), (PM) and (FTC), are exactly the frozen statements of the siblings plane_measure and halfspace_ftc. So (HB) applied to these two siblings and to P, d, v gives, for every test d-form φ and every t ∈ ℝ,
   (b) ∫_{V₀∩H_t} dφ(y)(v) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{L_t} φ(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y).
   For fixed φ, statement (b) for all t is exactly the hypothesis (HS) of (BZ). So (BZ) applied to P, d, v and φ gives
   (a) ∫_{V₀} dφ(y)(v) dHⁿ(y) = 0.

1. (Representation of C.) Let μ := θ₀·(Hⁿ⌞V₀), with scalar ENNReal.ofReal θ₀. Let ξ_v ∈ Λ_n be evaluation at v, ξ_v(α) := α(v_0, …, v_d) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v), and ξ(x) := ξ_v for all x.
   (a′) μ is finite on compact sets. (PM)(iii) with m := n, w := v, a := 0 gives Hⁿ(V₀ ∩ K) < ∞, because {y : y − 0 ∈ V₀} = V₀. Hence μ(K) = θ₀Hⁿ(V₀ ∩ K) < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top).
   (b′) ξ is constant, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Since v is orthonormal, (O1) gives |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(v)| ≤ |α| for every α.
   (c′) For every test n-form ω, ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) = (ENNReal.ofReal θ₀).toReal·∫_{V₀}ω(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀∫_{V₀}ω(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = C(ω) (integral_smul_measure, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with θ₀ ≥ 0).

2. (∂C = 0 and its representation.) For a test d-form η, ∂C(η) = C(dη) = θ₀∫_{V₀}dη(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀·0 = 0, by (a) of step 0 applied to η. Take μ′ := 0 and ξ′ := 0.
   - μ′ is finite.
   - ξ′ is constant.
   - The bound holds because μ′-a.e. statements are vacuous for μ′ = 0; it also holds pointwise, since |0| = 0 ≤ |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg).
   - ∫ξ′(x)(η(x))dμ′ = 0 = ∂C(η) (integral_zero_measure).

3. (The slicing function.) f(y) := ⟨y, v_0⟩ is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul). By Cauchy–Schwarz (abs_real_inner_le_norm) and ‖v_0‖ = 1, |f(y) − f(y′)| = |⟨y − y′, v_0⟩| ≤ ‖y − y′‖·‖v_0‖ = ‖y − y′‖.

4. (Slices from (SL).) Apply (SL) with:
   - U := ℝ^P (open), k := d and T := C;
   - the data (μ, ξ) and (μ′, ξ′) of steps 1–2, finite on compact subsets of U by step 1(a′);
   - f of step 3 and L := 1.
   This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ′(x)(η(x))dμ′(x) for all t and all test forms. Only these two formulas are used.

5. (Integer multiplicity from ISP.) Steps 1–3 are exactly the hypotheses of ISP for (μ, ξ), (μ′, ξ′), f and L = 1. So there is an L¹-null set N such that, for t ∉ N, every pair (A, B) with these two integral formulas has ∂A − B of integer multiplicity. For t ∉ N the pair (A_t, B_t) of step 4 qualifies, so Z := ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity. In Lean this is filter_upwards on the ∀ᵐ t given by ISP.

6. (Formula for Z.) Fix t ∉ N and a test d-form φ.
   - By the contract's subtraction of currents and ∂A(φ) = A(dφ), Z(φ) = A_t(dφ) − B_t(φ).
   - B_t(φ) = ∫ … d(μ′⌞{f<t}) = 0, since μ′ = 0 (Measure.restrict_zero, integral_zero_measure).
   - The half-space {f < t} = H_t is open (isOpen_lt), hence Borel. So μ⌞{f<t} = θ₀·Hⁿ⌞({f<t} ∩ V₀) (Measure.restrict_smul, Measure.restrict_restrict).
   - By integral_smul_measure and ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, then (b) of step 0 with Set.inter_comm,
     A_t(dφ) = θ₀∫_{V₀∩H_t} dφ(y)(v)dHⁿ(y) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(Fin.tail v)dH^d(y).
   Hence Z(φ) = θ₀∫_{L_t}φ(y)(Fin.tail v)dH^d(y) for every test d-form φ and every t ∉ N, that is, for L¹-almost every t. ∎
proof_key_steps: Step 0: halfspace_boundary, applied to the siblings plane_measure and halfspace_ftc, gives the half-plane Stokes formula ∫_{V₀∩{⟨y,v_0⟩<t}} dφ(v) dHⁿ = ∫_{L_t} φ(Fin.tail v) dH^d for every φ and t; boundary_zero turns this into ∫_{V₀} dφ(v) dHⁿ = 0.
(θ₀Hⁿ⌞V₀, constant evaluation at v) is an admissible representation of C: local finiteness by plane_measure (iii), the bound by covector_eval_le, the formula by integral_smul_measure.
∂C = 0 by step 0, so (0, 0) represents ∂C; f = ⟨·, v_0⟩ is 1-Lipschitz.
(SL) gives slices A_t, B_t with the two integral formulas; ISP makes Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t integer multiplicity for a.e. t.
Z_t(φ) = A_t(dφ) − 0 = θ₀∫_{V₀∩{⟨y,v_0⟩<t}} dφ(v) dHⁿ = θ₀∫_{L_t} φ(Fin.tail v) dH^d by step 0.
